title: Essay examines false computer-checked proofs and checker soundness
summary: A newly published essay hosted at cr.yp.to examines how computer-checked proofs can be false when the proof checker itself has a soundness bug, a concern for formal-methods users working with systems such as Lean and Metamath. It is a technical critique rather than a report of a new compromise, and the supplied material does not identify a specific theorem or deployment that was fooled. The practical question raised is whether acceptance by one checker is enough evidence, given that independent verification and review can catch different failures.
